children: At the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit, stakeholders highlight pharmaceutical supply chains, medical innovation, investment and AI-driven healthcare as key areas for bilateral collaboration

Delhi Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh on 19 November 2026, invited US healthcare and pharmaceutical companies to bring advanced technologies to India at affordable prices, calling for stronger bilateral partnerships to improve healthcare access and strengthen the country's medical infrastructure. Addressing the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit organised by the Indo-American Chamber of Commerce (IACC) in New Delhi, he highlighted the potential of combining India's pharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities and healthcare workforce with US expertise in biomedical research, technology and regulatory systems.

"Indian doctors and the pharmaceutical industry have made a name for themselves across the world. I would urge the US representatives present here today and the pharmaceutical companies to come to India with your technology at affordable prices. We welcome you, and together we can work towards strengthening the healthcare sector and providing affordable facilities to our people," Dr Singh said. The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation across medicine supply chains, disease surveillance, cancer research, medical technology and patient access.

Addressing the session on Healthcare, Pharma and Life Sciences, Genessa Giorgi, Health Attaché and Regional Representative for South Asia at the US Embassy, highlighted the importance of strengthening pharmaceutical supply chains as a shared priority for both countries.

"India plays an integral role in the global pharmaceutical supply chain and is the world's largest provider of generic medicines," Giorgi said, noting that India supplies more than 40% of the generic medicines consumed in the US.

She highlighted the contribution of bilateral pharmaceutical trade to access to essential medicines for chronic conditions, including diabetes, heart disease and cancer, as well as antibiotics and cancer treatments.

Referring to the India-US Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET), Giorgi said both countries were working towards strengthening supply chains and improving their resilience against future disruptions. She also highlighted the SelectUSA initiative and referred to USD 20.2 billion in investments announced by the US in May, of which USD 19.1 billion was in Indian pharmaceuticals and other sectors.

The session also examined the role of innovation and investment in expanding healthcare capabilities. Henna Dhawan, Country Head, Public Affairs, Novartis India, said innovative medicines should be recognised for the breakthroughs they deliver rather than being assessed primarily through their costs.
"Healthcare is not a cost but an investment," Dhawan said.

Dr Bhuvnesh Shrivastava, Lead Corporate Affairs, OBU, AstraZeneca Pharma India, identified portfolio diversification and innovation-focused partnerships as important drivers of pharmaceutical industry growth. He said companies needed to expand their portfolios and strengthen collaborations to respond to evolving healthcare requirements.

Regulatory preparedness amid technological advancement also emerged as a key discussion point. Ashish Kothari, Partner, Kochhar & Co, called for closer integration of artificial intelligence and legal frameworks as AI-based technologies increasingly enter medical diagnosis. He highlighted the need to address questions of accountability and liability alongside technological adoption. "Technology is catching up, so law also needs to catch up," Kothari said.

Other participants included Dr Sanjeev K Singh, Medical Director, Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences; Ravi Praful Valia, Director, Government Affairs, India Medtronic; and Gaurav Kaithwas, Director (Operations), UP Promote Pharma Council. The session was chaired by Dr Lokendra Gupta, Director, Emergency Medicine and Trauma Care, Vedanta Lucknow and President, SACTEM. The discussions underscored the scope for India-US collaboration in healthcare innovation, pharmaceutical manufacturing, investment and technology, with affordable access remaining a central consideration.
